newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends higher on technical fund buying.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends higher on technical fund buying.

text.p: COMEX copper ended higher on technical-based fund buying, flying in the face of fundamentals, in the view of many traders.

The funds appeared to take their cue from the London Metal Exchange technical resistance of $2,320 a tonne in the three-month contract, according to Mo Ahmadzadeh, president of Rudolf Wolff & Co, which corresponded to buy stops in New York at 108.10 cents a lb in the September contract.
September settled at 108.10 cents a lb, up 1.90 cents from Wednesday, while the spot month ended at 107.70 cents a lb, up 1.70 cents.
Fundamentally, most traders remain bearish, expecting higher inventories and weaker demand from Asia.
London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks increased another 800 tonnes to 245,775 tonnes in Thursday's report.

"The stock decline was a little less than expected and a little less than what we've seen in the last few weeks," said James Steel, analyst with Refco Inc. "That provided some support in the market. But ultimately the fundamentals played little role today."
LME stocks are expected to increase 20,000-40,000 tonnes a month through the end of the year, according to one large physical trader.
"It's not that business is bad. Business is pretty good, but there's a lot of supply coming on stream and we are going to feel the effects of that in the second half of the year," he said.
"All throughout the first half of the year, physical traders have been participating in Chilean tenders expecting the Chinese to come to the party," he said. "Guess what? It never happened."

Wolff's Ahmadzadeh remains optimistic, however. "I think you'll find that a lot of the LME stock increase we've seen in the last several weeks has been lent to the market, because of the backwardation," he said. "Come the fourth quarter, I would expect to see LME stocks declining."
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
